note: Primitive camping on an open grass flat beside the gravel parking lot midway along the access road, about 25 m from a small borrow-pit pond that the spot looks straight onto. The boat ramp to the Bates County Drainage Ditch is a separate lot at the end of the road, about 500 m on. The access road passes beneath the I-49 river bridges on the bank of the Marais des Cygnes River; no clearance is published. No facilities, and spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' - one mapped Primitive Camping symbol and GIS point on open grass beside the mid-road gravel lot (not the ramp lot); free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Pond kept (open ~25 m to a ~1-acre borrow pit). Pin fine. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays): the area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites' and says 'The area contains a boat ramp, primitive camping, two streams ..., "borrow pits," and an oxbow lake'. The 11/8/2022 map draws a Primitive Camping symbol beside the first Parking Lot on Old Town Access Rd, and GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point (OBJECTID 46) there, 56 m from that lot's centre and ~490 m from the boat-ramp lot. So the camping is a designated point on open ground beside a lot, not the ramp lot.

FIT: gravel road ~1 km from the East Service Rd to a ~25 x 30 m gravel lot with open grass beside it - a 23-ft rig fits. QUESTION: the access road passes UNDER the twin I-49 bridges on the riverbank (seen on imagery at ~38.1416,-94.3520); MDC's page posts no clearance and I found none (the Overpass mirror timed out, so OSM tags are unread). The ramp is used with boat trailers, but the clearance for a rig just under 10.5 ft is unverified - caveat written in the note.

WATERFRONT (stored pond, kept): the camping point sits on open mown/grass ground; a borrow-pit pond ~130 m x 40 m (about 1.2 acres - a pond under the 5-acre rule) lies ~25 m south with nothing but grass between, measured on the 0.33 m/px leaf-off frame. The road and lot are on the other (north) side. The Marais des Cygnes River is ~80 m north across the road behind a wooded bank (not in view) and the oxbow lake ~60 m west beyond trees. The stored waterfront_evidence was not shown in the dossier; the value holds on this read.
